title: GWAS and random forest give a 5-SNP sex identification panel for Pacific white shrimp
summary: In 1,244 Penaeus vannamei with a 55K SNP array, GWAS found 18 genome-wide significant SNPs and 10 candidate genes. A random forest 5-SNP panel was robust to simulated genotyping errors and missing data and gave 100% accuracy in two independent mixed-sex populations (ZJ, HN) and identified all females in an all-female cohort (MK). It is a marker panel, not a mechanism of sex determination.
ai_technology: Random Forest classification on GWAS-selected SNPs
organization: Yellow Sea Fisheries Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Fishery Sciences

evidence.tested: Evaluation in independent populations ZJ, HN and MK.
evidence.unknown: Panel performance in other populations is not reported; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Built the multi-SNP sex prediction model.
